summary: A merchandiser takes a buyer's garment order from enquiry to shipment: costing, samples, fabric and trims, production follow-up and delivery. It is one of the best-known career routes in the readymade garment (RMG) industry, open to textile, business and other graduates with strong English. This page shows pay ranges, skills, employers, a CV guide and a free skill test.

Mobile allowance, meals and yearly salary review in many circulars

Buying houses and liaison offices of international brands and retailers

Accessories, trims, packaging and washing companies

faq.q: What is the salary of a merchandiser in Bangladesh?
faq.a: Roughly BDT 15,000-35,000 a month for entry level, BDT 40,000-90,000 for mid level and BDT 100,000-200,000+ for senior roles. These are ranges from circulars, job posts and press reports checked on 16 Nov 2026. Many circulars say negotiable, so confirm in the actual circular.

faq.q: Can I become a merchandiser without a textile degree?
faq.a: Yes. Many circulars accept any bachelor's degree. A Business Standard interview (2020) said graduates of any subject can enter if their English is fluent, though they may need longer to learn the job than textile graduates.

faq.q: What does a merchandiser do every day?
faq.a: A merchandiser handles buyer emails, samples, costing, fabric and trims purchase, production follow-up and shipment planning. The job is to deliver the right product at the agreed price and date.

faq.q: What is the difference between a factory merchandiser and a buying house merchandiser?
faq.a: A factory merchandiser works for the manufacturer and manages buyer accounts. A buying house or liaison office merchandiser works on the buyer's side, checking price, quality and delivery across factories.

faq.q: What skills do I need to be a merchandiser?
faq.a: Strong business English, costing, tech pack reading, TNA follow-up, MS Excel and negotiation. Knowledge of fabrics, trims and quality terms (such as AQL) helps.
It can be busy near shipment dates and when buyers change requests. Good planning, written confirmations and a regular rest day help. Pressure differs by company and buyer.

faq.q: How long does it take to become a Senior Merchandiser?
faq.a: Circulars for senior merchandiser roles often ask for about 5-7 years of experience, while managers often need 7-14 years. Your path depends on your buyers, results and company.

faq.q: How do I avoid overseas job scams?
faq.a: Never pay a visa or job guarantee fee to an individual. Verify any recruiting agency with the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment and BMET before you pay or hand over a passport.

body_md:
**By [Daloyar Hassan Shishir](https://www.dhshishir.com)** · Career consultant, founder of Career Solutions and HereWeGrow · Facts last checked: 16 November 2026

> **Quick answer:** A garment merchandiser is the person who takes a buyer's order from enquiry to shipment. Entry pay is usually BDT 15,000-35,000 a month, mid-level BDT 40,000-90,000 and senior BDT 100,000-200,000+. The core skills are English, costing, tech pack reading, follow-up and negotiation. You can enter with a textile, fashion, business or any other degree if your English and numbers are strong.

## Merchandiser career at a glance

| Question | Short answer |
|---|---|
| Who hires? | Garment factories, buying houses and liaison offices of foreign brands, accessories and washing companies, some retail and packaging firms |
| Job titles in circulars | Assistant Merchandiser, Junior Merchandiser, Merchandiser, Sr. Merchandiser, Merchandising Manager, Head of Merchandising |
| Minimum education | A bachelor's degree. Textile, fashion or apparel degrees help, but many circulars accept any discipline |
| Must-have tools | MS Excel, email, costing sheets, tech pack reading, Time and Action (TNA) calendar, ERP where used |
| Licence or exam? | None. Professional diplomas (for example a postgraduate diploma in apparel merchandising) are optional |
| Key fact | RMG exports were US$38.70 billion in FY2025-26 (EPB), so orders and merchandisers are needed all year |
| Global demand | Every global brand that sources garments needs merchandisers on the supplier side and the buying side |

## What does a merchandiser do?

A merchandiser is the bridge between the buyer, the suppliers and the factory. One newspaper interview describes it exactly that way: "Merchandisers work as the bridge between the buyers, suppliers and the manufacturing facilities" (Saiful Islam Khan, The Business Standard, 2020). In simple words, you win the order, price it, get the samples approved, buy the fabric and trims, push production, and make sure the shipment leaves on time.

**A normal day:** check buyer emails, update the TNA calendar, chase a fabric supplier, review a sample comment with the sample room, send a costing revision, call the factory floor about a delay, and report order status to your manager. Evenings can be busy near shipment dates.

> "The ability to go beyond the book helps to become a successful merchandiser." (Md Shakhawat Hossain, quoted in The Business Standard, 2020)

## Scope: where this career can take you

Merchandising is a doorway into the whole garment business:

- **Factory merchandising:** you work directly for a manufacturer and manage buyer accounts.
- **Buying house or liaison office:** you work for the buyer's side, checking price, quality and delivery across many factories.
- **Product development and sampling:** you specialise in new styles, fabrics and costing.
- **Sourcing and supply chain:** fabric, trims and logistics planning.
- **Marketing and business development:** winning new buyers.
- **Management:** merchandising manager, head of merchandising, general manager, director.
- **Compliance and sustainability coordination:** buyers increasingly ask suppliers for audit and ESG documents.
- **Business owner:** one senior merchandiser interviewed by The Business Standard rose from merchandiser to merchandise manager, to chief operating officer, and later to factory owner. That is one person's path, not a promise.
- **Abroad:** global brands also run sourcing teams in other garment-producing countries. We have no verified count of Bangladeshi merchandisers abroad, so treat it as a possibility, not a plan.

## Salary in Bangladesh (2026 ranges)

| Level | Typical experience | Monthly pay (BDT) | Visual |
|---|---|---|---|
| Entry (Trainee, Assistant, Junior) | 0-3 years | 15,000 - 35,000 | ██ |
| Mid (Merchandiser, Sr. Merchandiser) | 4-8 years | 40,000 - 90,000 | █████ |
| Senior (Manager, GM, Head) | 10+ years | 100,000 - 200,000+ | ███████████ |

**How we got these ranges.** Public pay sites disagree, and many circulars simply say "negotiable", so we cross-checked press reports with the circulars and job posts that show numbers. A BDJobs assistant merchandiser post (BSc Textile, 3+ years, garments or buying house) offered Tk 25,000-30,000 with two festival bonuses. A recent hiring post for a buying-office team listed BDT 30,000-40,000 for junior merchandisers with 3-4 years and BDT 60,000-70,000 for senior merchandisers with 6-7 years. A trainee-to-merchandiser post for a Dhaka apparel firm listed BDT 15,000-40,000. A home-textile merchandiser post at a multinational retailer's liaison office listed around BDT 90,000 plus benefits. A BDJobs post for a General Manager (Marketing and Merchandising) listed Tk 100,000-200,000. The Business Standard (2020) reported starting pay of about Tk 15,000, mid-senior pay of about Tk 80,000 and senior pay above Tk 3,00,000 for a few top people. We did not use the Payscale pages because their figures swing wildly and mix units. These are ranges, not promises. Several of the circulars we read were not dated, and 2020 press figures are older, so confirm in the actual circular.

### Who pays the most?

As a general pattern, pay rises in this order: small factories and trading firms → mid-size local factories → large export groups → buying houses and liaison offices of foreign brands (usually the highest, often with stronger English and costing demands). Denim, sweater and woven specialists with strong buyer relationships can earn more than average. Your English, your accuracy and your track record of on-time shipments move pay more than your degree.

**Global comparison:** we did not find a reliable public merchandiser salary figure for other countries, so we leave it out rather than guess.

## Benefits beyond salary

- Festival bonuses (two a year is common in circulars; some offer three).
- Mobile allowance, lunch or snacks, and yearly salary review in many circulars.
- Provident fund, gratuity and medical insurance at some larger companies (for example a manager post at a bag exporter listed provident fund and gratuity).
- Travel to factories and, in some firms, buyer visits and fairs.
- A strong skill set that moves between companies and product types.

## Top employers: Bangladesh and the world

**Bangladesh: largest exporting groups.** Prothom Alo compiled the top exporting industrial groups for FY2024-25 from National Board of Revenue (NBR) data, excluding sample and deemed exports (published 4 November 2025). The first four were Youngone Corporation (about US$970 million), Ha-Meem Group (about US$650 million), Mondol Group (about US$560 million) and DBL Group (about US$520 million). Other groups in that top ten included Ananta, PRAN-RFL, Square, Palmal, Pacific Jeans and Micro Fibre. Some groups in the list also export non-garment goods. The article's smaller figures looked inconsistent, so check NBR data before quoting numbers beyond the first four.

**Other well-known garment groups** (alphabetical, not a ranking): Epyllion Group, Fakir Fashion, Square Fashions, Viyellatex. Always check a company's current status and recent news before applying.

**Buying houses and liaison offices:** many buying houses operate in Bangladesh. An older press report counted about 1,430 members of the buying house association, so treat that number as indicative only. Many liaison offices of international brands post merchandiser jobs on LinkedIn and BDJobs.

**Buyers (examples, not a ranking):** global brands and retailers such as H&M, Inditex, Primark, Marks & Spencer and C&A appear in public supplier-factory statistics. Global Sources reports that DBL's clients have included Levi's, Wrangler and American Eagle.

**A fact worth knowing:** estimates of the number of garment factories differ, from about 3,320 (Mapped in Bangladesh) to nearly 4,500 (BGMEA), as Dhaka Tribune reported. BGMEA's 2021 publication said the sector supports over 4 million jobs directly.

## Skills employers ask for

| Skill | Why it matters | Demand |
|---|---|---|
| Business English (email, calls) | Every buyer conversation | █████ |
| Costing and price negotiation | Wrong cost = lost profit | █████ |
| Tech pack and garment construction knowledge | Avoids sample errors | ████ |
| TNA planning and shipment follow-up | On-time delivery | █████ |
| MS Excel | Costing sheets, order tracking | █████ |
| Fabric, trims and knit/woven basics | Sourcing and quality | ████ |
| Quality and compliance awareness (AQL, buyer codes) | Buyers audit suppliers | ███ |
| ERP and digital tools | Large groups | ███ |
| Negotiation and calm under pressure | Late changes are normal | ████ |

*Demand bars are our reading of recent circulars, not a statistical survey.*

## Free ways to build these skills

- **Costing:** the ITC Global Textile Academy offers a free one-hour [Garment Costing course](https://globaltextileacademy.intracen.org/course/info.php?id=2637) with a certificate of completion.
- **Excel:** Microsoft's free help at [support.microsoft.com/excel](https://support.microsoft.com/excel).
- **Tech pack basics:** the free-to-learn [Fashion Design Essentials](https://www.mygreatlearning.com/academy/learn-for-free/courses/fashion-design-essentials) course on Great Learning covers tech pack basics (a certificate costs extra).
- **Industry knowledge:** [Textile Learner](https://textilelearner.net) is an informal learning site; use it for explanations and always cross-check with a real factory or buyer document.
- **Bangla e-learning:** [muktopaath.gov.bd](https://muktopaath.gov.bd).
- **Practice:** build a costing sheet in Excel for a basic T-shirt and a five-pocket trouser, with fabric, trims, CM (cutting and making), overhead and profit.

## Qualifications, scholarships and study support

| Route | Provider | Best for |
|---|---|---|
| Bachelor of Apparel Merchandising & Management (4 years, 140 credits) | [BUFT](https://buft.edu.bd/department-of-apparel-merchandising-and-management) | School leavers who want a direct route |
| Postgraduate Diploma in Apparel Merchandising (1 year) | [BUFT](https://buft.edu.bd) | Graduates from any subject who want to switch |
| BSc in textile, apparel or fashion fields | Textile universities such as [BUTEX](https://www.butex.edu.bd) and [NITER](https://niter.edu.bd) | Technical depth, strong in factory roles |
| Short courses in costing, Excel, business English | Free and paid online providers | Anyone, anytime |

BUFT's admission pages also list merchandising programmes (knitwear and woven) and scholarships. Fees, intake dates and rules change, so check the official site.

**Support to explore (check each official site for current rules):**

- **Chevening (UK):** [chevening.org](https://www.chevening.org) for a funded master's (supply chain, business or related fields).
- **Commonwealth Scholarships:** [cscuk.fcdo.gov.uk](https://cscuk.fcdo.gov.uk).
- **DAAD (Germany):** [daad.de](https://www.daad.de/en/).
- **Fulbright (USA):** through the US Embassy in Dhaka.
- **University scholarships:** ask BUFT, BUTEX and NITER about merit and need-based support.

## Long-term career timeline

| Years | Typical title | What to master |
|---|---|---|
| 0-2 | Trainee / Assistant Merchandiser | Samples, follow-up, TNA, Excel, English emails |
| 3-5 | Merchandiser | Costing, price negotiation, running 2-3 buyer accounts |
| 6-9 | Sr. Merchandiser / Assistant Manager | Large accounts, team support, buyer visits |
| 10-14 | Merchandising Manager / Head | Strategy, team leadership, buyer relationships |
| 15+ | GM / Director / Sourcing head / Founder | Business growth, governance, mentoring |

*A typical path, not a guarantee. It depends on buyers, orders and company growth.*

## Plan your own path (5-minute worksheet)

Copy these five lines and fill them in today:

1. **My level now:** (student / fresher / ___ years)
2. **My target title in 3 years:** ___
3. **Three skills I lack** (use the checklist on this page): ___, ___, ___
4. **One learning step this quarter:** (costing course / Excel / PGD / English practice)
5. **My weekly study hours and day:** ___ hours on ___

Then take the free skill test on this page and compare the result with line 3.

## Career shifts: where merchandisers move

- **Merchandiser → buying house merchandiser or buying office manager** (the buyer's side).
- **Merchandiser → product development or sourcing manager.**
- **Merchandiser → supply chain or planning.**
- **Merchandiser → compliance or sustainability coordinator** (add audit knowledge).
- **Merchandiser → business development and marketing.**
- **Merchandiser → sourcing agent or small garment business owner.**
- **Merchandiser → trainer or lecturer** (apparel merchandising departments need industry people).

## Where will you find more peace of mind?

No job is free of pressure, and we have no survey to rank them. As a general pattern, factory merchandising near shipment dates can mean long hours and urgent calls, buying offices often have steadier hours but strict reporting, and training or planning roles tend to have more predictable routines. Three habits protect your peace: keep your TNA calendar current every day, confirm every decision by email so nothing depends on memory, and protect one fixed rest day each week.

## Faith and history: honest trade

**The Quran.** Surah Al-Mutaffifin warns against cheating in measure and weight ([83:1-3 on quran.com](https://quran.com/83/1-3)). Surah Al-Ma'idah opens with the command to fulfil your contracts ([5:1](https://quran.com/5/1)). A buyer order is a contract of trust, and a merchandiser who keeps quality, price and delivery promises is practising that command. The longest verse of the Quran also instructs believers to write down agreements ([2:282](https://quran.com/2/282)), which is why a clean email trail matters.

**Hadith.** The Prophet (peace be upon him) said that whoever cheats us is not one of us (Sahih Muslim 101).

**History.** Classical biographies of the Prophet (peace be upon him) record that before prophethood he travelled for trade on behalf of Khadijah (may Allah be pleased with her) and was known for honesty. The lesson for a merchandiser is simple: your reputation with buyers is built one honest shipment at a time.

## Your contribution to the nation

Ready-made garments earned US$38.70 billion in FY2025-26, per Export Promotion Bureau data, and the sector makes up more than 80 percent of Bangladesh's exports (The Daily Star). Every order has a merchandiser behind it. When Bangladesh leaves the least developed country list on 24 November 2026, EU duty-free access is expected to continue until November 2029 under a transition period, after which exporters will need new trade arrangements. Skilled merchandisers who can win orders, control cost and meet buyer standards help protect jobs for millions of workers.

## Your contribution to the world

Clothes you help ship are worn in Europe, North America and beyond. Merchandisers also carry buyers' safety and ethical expectations into the factory. The RMG Sustainability Council covers about 1,766 factories and 2.8 million workers under the Bangladesh Safety Agreement (as of 30 September 2026). Merchandisers who plan realistic lead times, pay attention to fair buying practices and reduce waste make the whole chain safer and fairer. BGMEA's 2023 sustainability report found about 20,146 metric tons of waste across 57 reporting factories, including 16,545 tons of fabric off-cuts, so smarter planning and cutting plans matter.

## If you want to be an entrepreneur

- **Sourcing or buying agency** for small foreign brands (learn the work in a buying house first).
- **Freelance costing and tech pack service** for startup clothing brands.
- **Trims, labels or packaging supply** for factories.
- **Sample-making and small-batch production** for local fashion brands.
- **Garment trading or e-commerce brand sourcing** with tight quality control.
- **Training centre** for costing, Excel and merchandising skills.

Start small: two repeat customers and clean cash flow beat a big office.

## Research opportunities

- Topics with real need in Bangladesh: post-LDC trade strategy, lead-time reduction, fabric waste and circularity, buyer purchasing practices and supplier cost pressure, digital costing and ERP, women's career progression in merchandising.
- Where to learn and publish: apparel and textile faculties (BUFT, BUTEX, NITER), BGMEA research publications, and international trade and labour bodies.
- Path: a strong thesis or industry project → research assistant → MPhil/PhD (the scholarships above fund many of these).

## Whom to follow and learn from

Follow institutions first: [BGMEA](https://www.bgmea.com.bd), [BUFT](https://buft.edu.bd), [BUTEX](https://www.butex.edu.bd), [NITER](https://niter.edu.bd), [RMG Sustainability Council](https://rsc-bd.org), [Better Work Bangladesh](https://betterwork.org/bangladesh/our-services/) and the [ITC Global Textile Academy](https://globaltextileacademy.intracen.org). On LinkedIn, follow merchandising and sourcing heads of the companies you want to join and read what they post about hiring.

## Where to find merchandiser jobs

- [BDJobs](https://www.bdjobs.com) (Garments/Textile category) and company career pages.
- LinkedIn Jobs and hiring posts by buying offices and factories.
- Factory and group websites, and company hiring pages of large exporters.
- BUFT and other university career or placement offices.

> **Warning on overseas jobs:** never pay a "visa fee" or "job guarantee" fee to an individual. Press reports describe workers cheated by brokers and agencies even when they held BMET clearance, and the Ministry of Expatriates' Welfare and Overseas Employment has told people not to pay money before an official announcement of a new recruitment market. Verify any recruiting agency with the ministry and BMET before you pay or hand over a passport.

## Merchandiser CV: what to write

Your CV should show buyers, products, volumes, on-time shipments and software, not only duties.

| Weak line | Better line |
|---|---|
| Handled buyer orders. | Managed 3 knit buyer accounts, about 40 orders a season, from costing to shipment. |
| Responsible for sampling. | Cut sample approval time by planning comments with the pattern room and tracking them on a TNA sheet. |
| Good at costing. | Prepared FOB costing sheets in Excel and negotiated trims cost, saving about 4% on one order. |

*Use only your real, provable figures. Replace every example above with your own.*

**Computer skills for the CV:** name the tools (Excel costing and tracking sheets, email, ERP if any, Photoshop or Illustrator if you use them). Do not write "MS Office" alone.

**Career objective samples:**

- *Fresher:* "BBA graduate with strong English and Excel skills seeking an Assistant Merchandiser role to support sample development, costing and shipment follow-up."
- *Experienced:* "Merchandiser with 5 years in knit garments, skilled in costing, buyer communication and on-time shipment, seeking a Senior Merchandiser role."

Build yours free with the HereWeGrow CV Builder and the Merchandiser CV template.

## Common mistakes in applications

- Listing duties without buyers, products or numbers.
- Writing "MS Office" instead of named tools.
- Ignoring the circular's experience, age or document request.
- Weak English in the cover email. Proofread before you send.
- Sending a file named "CV final 2". Use YourName_Merchandiser_CV.pdf.
- Claiming costing or tech pack skills you cannot show in the interview.

growth_plan.y1: Learn Excel costing, tech packs, TNA and sample stages; take the free costing course; complete one internship or first assistant role; practise English emails daily.
growth_plan.y2: Run two or three orders alone, build supplier and buyer follow-up habits, learn fabric and trims sourcing, and keep a record of on-time shipments and savings.
growth_plan.y3: Move to Merchandiser or Senior Merchandiser, handle costing negotiation and a buyer account, learn quality and compliance basics, and consider a diploma or MBA if you want management roles.

goal_sheet: Week 1-2: Excel basics (SUM, IF, VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, tables)
Week 3-4: Learn garment parts, knit vs woven, and read two sample tech packs
Month 2: Take the free garment costing course and build a costing sheet for a T-shirt
Month 3: Draw a TNA calendar for a mock order and practise sample stages
Month 4: Learn FOB, L/C, lead time and buyer communication; write 20 practice emails
Month 5: Basic quality terms (AQL, inspection) and compliance awareness
Month 6: Update CV, write cover letter, apply to 10 circulars, practise 20 interview questions

options: A document with a style's design details, measurements, materials and construction
test.explain: A tech pack tells the factory exactly how to make a style.

test.q: Under FOB terms, the seller is responsible until the goods are:
options: Loaded on board the ship at the named port
test.explain: FOB (Free On Board) ends the seller's cost and risk once goods are loaded on the vessel.

test.q: A TNA (Time and Action) calendar is used to:
options: Track every milestone from order to shipment with dates
test.explain: It lists tasks, owners and deadlines so delays are seen early.

test.q: In garment costing, CM usually means:
test.explain: CM covers the cost of cutting and making the garment in the factory.

test.q: GSM on a fabric specification stands for:
test.explain: GSM shows fabric weight, which affects feel, cost and use.

test.q: Single jersey fabric, used for most T-shirts, is made by:
test.explain: Jersey is a knit fabric; woven fabric is used for shirts and trousers.
The PP sample confirms fit, trims and quality before bulk cutting.

test.q: AQL is used in inspection to decide:
options: The acceptable quality limit for a sampled lot
test.explain: AQL sets how many defects are acceptable when a sample is inspected.

test.q: One shirt needs 1.5 m of fabric including wastage. How much fabric is needed for 2,000 shirts?
A letter of credit (L/C) is best described as:
options: A bank's promise to pay the seller when the stated documents are presented

cv_template_notes: Use the HWG Merchandiser CV (clean, one-column layout for easy reading by HR). Put buyers, products and volumes at the top of each job (for example knit basics, 3 buyer accounts, about 40 orders a season) and name software and tools (Excel costing sheets, ERP, any design tool). Show on-time shipment, cost savings or sample approval results only if you can prove them. Include your English level and any costing or merchandising course. Keep it to 2 pages. File name: YourName_Merchandiser_CV.pdf.
cover_letter_md:
Dear Hiring Manager,

I am applying for the Assistant Merchandiser position advertised on [site/date]. I have [X] years of experience in [sample follow-up, costing and shipment planning] and use Excel for costing and order tracking. In my last role I [one provable result, e.g. kept 95% of orders on time across 3 buyers].

I communicate clearly in English with buyers and suppliers and keep every decision in writing. I would be glad to bring this discipline to [Company name].

Thank you for your time. I have attached my CV and would welcome an interview.

Sincerely,
[Your name]
[Phone] | [Email]
interview_qs: Tell me about yourself. (Tip: 45 seconds: education, one relevant skill or project, why merchandising.)
Why do you want to be a merchandiser? (Tip: Show you understand it is a follow-up and communication job, not only a desk job.)
Explain the full process of an order from enquiry to shipment. (Tip: Enquiry, costing, sample, approval, PO, fabric and trims booking, production, inspection, shipment, payment.)
What is a tech pack and what does it contain? (Tip: Design sketch, measurement chart, BOM, construction, labels and packing details.)
How do you prepare a costing for a basic T-shirt? (Tip: Fabric, trims, CM, overhead, wastage, profit; mention consumption.)
What is FOB and how is it different from CIF or ex-factory? (Tip: Keep it simple and use a one-line example.)
What does CM mean and how is it calculated? (Tip: Cutting and making charge; mention SMV and efficiency only if you know them.)
What is a TNA calendar and how do you use it? (Tip: Give a real or mock example with dates.)
What are the different types of samples? (Tip: Proto, fit, size set, salesman, PP, TOP, shipment sample, as used in your experience.)
What is the difference between knit and woven garments? (Tip: Give two product examples of each.)
What is GSM and why does it matter? (Tip: Fabric weight, affects cost, feel and use.)
How do you calculate fabric consumption? (Tip: Use a simple pieces x consumption x wastage example.)
What is lead time and how do you protect it? (Tip: Early booking, regular follow-up, written approvals.)
The buyer changes the order quantity after fabric is booked. What do you do? (Tip: Check impact, inform manager, confirm in writing, discuss cost and date.)
A fabric supplier says delivery will be 10 days late. What is your plan? (Tip: Assess impact, check alternatives, inform the buyer early, update TNA.)
How do you handle a buyer who rejects a sample three times? (Tip: Stay calm, list comments clearly, agree a correction plan with the pattern room.)
How do you negotiate price with a supplier? (Tip: Compare quotes, quantity, payment terms; never reveal your target first.)
What is AQL? (Tip: Acceptable quality limit; say it controls defects in a sampled lot.)
What is a letter of credit and why do exporters use it? (Tip: Bank guarantee of payment against documents.)
What documents are needed for a shipment? (Tip: Invoice, packing list, bill of lading or airway bill, certificate of origin where required, as per your experience.)
How do you manage more than one buyer account at a time? (Tip: Priorities, daily tracker, weekly review.)
What Excel functions do you use at work? (Tip: Name real ones: VLOOKUP/XLOOKUP, SUMIF, pivot table, IF.)
What is the difference between a factory merchandiser and a buying house merchandiser? (Tip: Show you know both viewpoints.)
What is a compliance audit and how does it affect your job? (Tip: Buyers check safety, labour and environment; delays can happen if the factory fails.)
How do you work with the production and quality teams? (Tip: Give an example of a meeting or follow-up system.)
Tell me about a time you made a mistake in an order. (Tip: Be honest, explain the fix and what you changed.)
How do you handle pressure near the shipment date? (Tip: Planning, priority list, honest early alerts.)
What do you know about our company and its buyers? (Tip: Read the website and recent news before the interview.)
What is your expected salary? (Tip: Give a range based on the circular and your skills; stay polite and flexible.)
Where do you see yourself in five years? (Tip: Name a role and the skills you will build, such as costing and buyer handling.)
